newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran, Iraq to swap bodies of soldiers killed in war.
newsitem.headline: Iran, Iraq to swap bodies of soldiers killed in war.

text.p: Iran and Iraq will on Sunday exchange the bodies of 87 soldiers killed during their 1980-88 war, the official Iranian news agency IRNA said on Saturday.
It quoted General Mir-Faisal Baqerzadeh, head of Iran's committee for the missing in action, as saying the remains of 20 Iranians would be exchanged for those of 67 Iraqi soldiers.
He said the swap would take place at the Khosrawi border checkpoint in northwestern Iran.

Both sides have swapped prisoners of war and remains of soldiers. But the missing in action and the POWs are still among the thorniest issues hindering efforts to improve ties between the former foes.
Iran has said 5,000 to 10,000 prisoners are held by Iraq. Baghdad denies holding any Iranians and says more than 20,000 Iraqis are held by Tehran.
In Baghdad, Iraq's most influential newspaper Babel urged Iran's President-Elect Mohammad Khatami to work for the normalisation of ties.

Babel, owned by President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday, told Khatami that his landslide victory in presidential elections was a message to him to introduce changes in Iran's policy both on the domestic and international levels.
